entry.name: function
entry.description: Draw or store a set of x, y points as floating-point numbers. The output the entire function is useful as an input for line~. You can also get an interpolated y value for any x value.

attributes.name: autosustain
attributes.description: Sets the sustain mode for. There are three possible values: 'Off', 'Next-to-Last Point', and 'Any Single Point'. The default is 0 (off).

choices.label: The next-to-last point in the function is automatically a sustain point. This setting requires that there are more than two points in the current function.
Allows you to click on any point in the function to make it a sustain point. Ifis on and there is already a different point that is a sustain point, that other point will be turned off.

attributes.name: clickadd
attributes.description: Toggles a user's ability to create new breakpoints by clicking and dragging with the mouse. This feature is enabled by default.

attributes.name: clickmove
attributes.description: Toggles a user's ability to move existing breakpoints by dragging them with the mouse. This feature is enabled by default.

attributes.name: clicksustain
attributes.description: Theattribute controls how you can specify sustain points with your mouse. There are three possible values: off, cmd/ctrl click, and double-click. The default value is 2 (double-click).

choices.label: The ability to specify sustain points with your mouse is turned off.
Specify sustain points by pressing Cmd/Ctrl and clicking with your mouse.
Specify sustain points by double-clicking with your mouse.

attributes.name: mode
attributes.description: Sets whether the function includes curve information. This changes both the function display and output format. When curve information is not included, the format of the second outlet is compatible with theandobjects. When curve information is included, the output is compatible with theobject.

choices.label: No curve information is included or displayed

attributes.name: mousereport
attributes.description: When enabled, the third outlet sends a three item list containing the current cursor position as well as the index of the current point under cursor (or -1 if the cursor is not over a point). Output occurs when the cursor is over the object in a locked patcher.

attributes.name: outputmode
attributes.description: When enabled, the list sent out the second outlet includes the X coordinate of the first point of the function. By defaultis disabled for compatibility with theandobjects that expect a list that starts with the initial Y (target) value.

The menu displays all available parameters of compatible objects.Setting theattribute with a message requires the target parameter's path, which is the host object's scriping name followed by two colons and the parameter name. For example, for aobject with scripting name, the path of theparameter would be. You can set a value for thebefore the host object or parameter exists, and the object will connect to the parameter once it exists. Refer to the user guide entry forfor more details.

attributes.name: shadowreflectionpoint

messages.name: (mouse)
messages.description: You can use the mouse to add or edit breakpoints.

messages.name: bang
messages.description: Triggers a list output of the current breakpoints from the middle-left outlet formatted for use by theobject. As an example, if thecontained breakpoints at X = 1, Y = 0; X = 10, Y = 1; and X = 20, Y = 0, the output would be. If the optional output mode is enabled, the output would be.If there are any sustain points in the function,outputs a list of all the points up to the sustain point. Additional points in the function, up to a subsequent sustain point or the end point, whichever applies, can be output by sending the next message. See the description of theandmessages for additional information.

messages.name: clear
messages.description: The wordby itself erases all existing breakpoints. The wordcan also be followed by one or more breakpoint indices (starting at 0) to clear selected breakpoints.

messages.name: clearfix
messages.description: The wordclears all fix states (sets them to 0).

messages.name: clearsustain
messages.description: The wordclears all sustain states (sets them to 0).

messages.name: color
messages.description: Themessage sets a color with an index from 0 to 15 for breakpoints and lines against a light background. It is no longer supported.

messages.name: copy
messages.digest: Copy the points from a function
messages.description: Themessage copies all of the current function points to the clipboard so that they can be pasted into anotherobject.

messages.name: dump
messages.description: Outputs a series of multiple element lists describing each break point out theobject's third outlet. Each list contains the breakpoints X and Y values, followed by the curve value, if present. An optional symbol argument can be used to specify aobjects as a destination.

messages.name: fix
messages.description: The word, followed by a number specifying the index of a point and 0 or 1, prevents the user from changing the point if the second number is 1, and allows the user to change the point if the second number is 0. By default, points are moveable unless clickmove 0 has been sent to disable moving of all points.

messages.name: float
messages.description: The value is taken as an X value and outputs a corresponding Y value out the left outlet. The Y value is produced by linear floating-point interpolation of the function. If the X value lies outside the first or last breakpoint, the Y value is.

messages.name: getfix
messages.description: The word. with no arguments, will cause theobject to send a list all fix points out the object's third outlet. If an index is provided as an argument, the fix state for that point will be output.

messages.name: getsustain
messages.description: The word. with no arguments, will cause theobject to send a list all sustain points out the object's third outlet. If an index is provided as an argument, the sustain state for that point will be output.

messages.name: int
messages.description: The value is taken as an X value and outputs a corresponding Y value out the left outlet. The Y value is produced by linear floating-point interpolation of the function. If the X value lies outside the first or last breakpoint, the Y value is.

messages.name: lineout
messages.description: The wordfollowed by either 0, 1, or no argument is equivalent to themessage.

messages.name: list
messages.description: If the list contains two values, a new point is added to the function. The first value is X, the second is Y.If the list contains three values, an existing point in theis modified. The first value is the index (starting at 0) of a breakpoint to modify, the second is the new X value for the breakpoint, and the third is the new Y value for the breakpoint. (If the index number in the list refers to a breakpoint that does not exist, the message is ignored.)If the list contains four values and the mode attribute is set to 1 (curve), the third value is the curve amount, with values greater than 0 resulting an exponential curve, and values less than 0 resulting in a logarithmic curve.

messages.name: listdump
messages.digest: Output all breakpoints as a single list
messages.description: Outputs a single list which contains all X and Y values for each of the breakpoints out theobject's third outlet. An optional symbol argument can be used to specify aobject as a destination.

messages.name: next
messages.description: Themessage sends a list out the second outlet that continues from the sustain point where the output of the last bang or next message ended. For instance, if thecontained breakpoints at (a) X = 1, Y = 0; (b) X = 10, Y = 1; and (c) X = 20, Y = 0, and point b was a sustain point, amessage would outputand a subsequentmessage would outputAfter amessage reaches the end point, a subsequentmessage is equivalent to amessage.is also equivalent to awhen nohas been sent that reached a sustain point, or when acontains no sustain points.

messages.name: nth
messages.description: The word, followed by a number, uses the number as the index (starting at 0) of a breakpoint, and outputs the Y value of the breakpoint out the left outlet. If no breakpoint with the specified index exists, no output occurs.

messages.name: paste
messages.digest: Paste the points of a copied function
messages.description: Themessage pastes all of the points of a previously copied function into aobject.

messages.name: quantize_x
messages.digest: Quantize points on the grid's horizontal axis
messages.description: This message will cause all of the points to automatically snap to the horizontal grid as defined by theattribute.

messages.name: quantize_y
messages.digest: Quantize points on the grid's vertical axis
messages.description: This message will cause all of the points to automatically snap to the vertical grid as defined by theattribute.

messages.name: set
messages.description: Given the number of points already defined within's graphic editor, a corresponding list of x-y-coordinate pairs will set the position of each point.

messages.name: setcurve
messages.digest: Draw a curve between two points
messages.description: The word, followed by an integer that specifies the index of a function point (numbered from 1) and a floating point value that specifies a curve, will create a curved line segment between the specified point and the next point.Curve factor values from 0 to 1.0 produce an "exponential" curve when increasing in value and values from -1.0 to 0 produce a "logarithmic" curve. The closer to 0 the curve parameter is, the closer the curve is to a straight line, and the farther away the parameter is from 0, the steeper the curve. Theattribute must be set to 1 (curve mode) for this message to be effective.

messages.name: setdomain
messages.description: The word, followed by aorvalue, sets the maximum displayed X value, then modifies the X values of all breakpoints so that they remain in the same place given the new domain.

messages.name: setrange
messages.digest: Set minimum and maximum Y-axis values
messages.description: The word, followed by twoorvalues, sets the minimum and maximum display range for Y values, then modifies the Y values of all breakpoints so that they remain in the same place given the new range.

messages.name: sustain
messages.digest: Set the sustain state for a breakpoint
messages.description: The word, followed by number specifying the index of a point and zero or one, turns that point into a sustain point if the second number is 1, or into a regular point if the second number is 0. By default, points are regular (non-sustain). The behavior of sustain points is discussed in the description of themessage above. Command-clicking on Macintosh or Control-clicking on Windows also toggle the sustain property of a point.

messages.name: xyc
messages.digest: Add a point with curve information
messages.description: The word, followed by an two numbers that specifies X and Y values and a floating point number that specifies a curve factor, will add a new point with curve information to the function.Curve factor values from 0 to 1.0 produce an "exponential" curve when increasing in value and values from -1.0 to 0 produce a "logarithmic" curve. The closer to 0 the curve parameter is, the closer the curve is to a straight line, and the farther away the parameter is from 0, the steeper the curve. Theattribute must be set to 1 (curve mode) for this message to be effective.

outlets.digest: Interpolated Y (float) for Input X Interpolated Y (float) for Input X
